title: Intermittent Degradation Handbook and Headroom Negotiation
author: Avery Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This handbook prescribes a standardized operational approach for diagnosing and recovering from intermittent degradation modes in model-serving paths (examples: increased 95th/99th tail latency, transient error spikes, and partial feature regressions). It couples tactical runbook steps with a negotiation procedure between SRE and Product/Platform teams to allocate short-term headroom using error budgets and capacity credits. The goal is rapid mitigation, controlled customer communication, and traceable decisions for post-incident analysis and capacity planning.

Scope
-----
Applies to: production inference stack (service names below) across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Primary services in scope: "infer-gateway", "runtime-pool-manager", "kv-cache", "batcher", and "model-allocator".
- Typical symptoms covered: recurring 95th/99th latency spikes lasting 1–30 minutes, sporadic increase in 5xxs with request patterns unchanged, and transient elevated token cost due to re-tries or cache misses.
- Out of scope: full region outages, hardware failures that trigger node-level OOMs (see oom-cascade-and-memory-throttling-runbook).

SLOs and Error Budget Rules
---------------------------
Primary SLOs to evaluate for intermittent degradations:
- infer-gateway latency (p95): 200ms (SLO)
- infer-gateway availability (5xx rate): <= 0.1% (SLO)
- batcher throughput: >= 90% of reserved throughput per-minute (SLO)

Error budget policy for short-term headroom:
1) If incident consumes < 5% of monthly error budget for the affected SLO, SRE may grant a temporary headroom credit (up to +20% token headroom or priority lane slots) for 1 hour after coordination with Product on the call.
2) If incident consumes 5–20% of monthly error budget, escalation to Platform PM and Capacity PM required; headroom may be granted only with a rollback/mitigation plan and limited to 30 minutes.
3) If > 20% consumed, invoke emergency capacity protocol and formal incident review; no ad-hoc credits without exec approval.

Detection and Triage
--------------------
Detection: dashboards and automated alerts should trigger for these signals:
- Latency spike: PromQL alert: 
```
sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"infer-gateway\",le=\"0.5\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job=\"infer-gateway\"}[5m])) > 0.95
```
- Error spike: 
```
increase(http_requests_total{job=\"infer-gateway\",status=~\"5..\"}[5m]) / increase(http_requests_total{job=\"infer-gateway\"}[5m]) > 0.001
```
- Cache miss storm: KV cache miss rate > 15% sustained for 3 minutes.

Initial triage checklist (first 10 minutes) — run in parallel:
1) Confirm alert validity (on-call checks Grafana panels and replays raw traces).
2) Identify scope: single model, single cluster, single region, or multi-tenant impact.
3) Correlate with deploys / rollouts in last 60 minutes (use CICD deploy logs).
4) Check model-allocator and runtime-pool-manager metrics: queue length, allocation failures, eviction counts.
5) If latency-only and no error-rate increase, consider transient backpressure or batching variance.
6) Determine initial mitigation path: scale (warm-pool / burst), degrade model fidelity, or throttling.

Runbook: Remediation Paths
-------------------------
Choose one primary path based on scope and customer impact. Always document decisions in the incident timeline with the reason and owner.

A) Fast capacity absorb (when token headroom is available)
1) Verify warm pool capacity: curl -s https://ops-api.internal/warm-pool/status | jq .pools
2) If warm pool slots free, trigger fast-attach: opsctl pool attach --service infer-gateway --count N (N = min(available, needed)).
3) Monitor token queue length and p95; if stable within 5 minutes, mark mitigation successful and start 1-hour headroom window.

B) Graceful degradation (when capacity or headroom not available)
1) Enable model fidelity downgrade (A/B style rollback to smaller variant): opsctl rollout pause && opsctl rollback --model-version v2-small --target infer-gateway
2) Activate prefix KV cache warmup: opsctl cache prewarm --models <list> --parallel 8
3) Shorten max-completion-len per-request via API feature flag for non-critical tenants.

C) Traffic shaping and tenant prioritization (multi-tenant incidence)
1) Open the priority ledger and apply temporary priority lanes: opsctl throttle --service infer-gateway --policy priority-lane.json
2) Notify affected mid-tier customers with templated message (see Communications).
3) If tenant-driven anomaly, apply tenant eviction rule for < 10 minutes and monitor SLO delta.

D) Fallback model routing (last-resort to preserve availability)
1) Route requests to a compatible but cheaper model variant using routing policy: POST /admin/routing/patch {"route":"fallback-v1","criteria":"latency>200ms"}
2) Observe quality metrics from Canary Eval set for 10 minutes; if quality impact acceptable, extend fallback with tickets to Product for roll-forward plan.

Operational Tooling Commands and Dashboards
-----------------------------------------
- Basic checks:
  - kubectl -n inference get pods --selector=app=infer-gateway
  - opsctl monitor traces -s infer-gateway --last 15m
- Capacity views (Grafana):
  - Cluster capacity dashboard: /grafana/d/cluster-capacity
  - Warm pool utilization: /grafana/d/warm-pools
- Emergency attach CLI: opsctl pool attach --service-infer-gateway --count 10 --reason "intermittent-degradation"

Communication templates
-----------------------
Internal (Slack brief) — single paragraph:
"[INCIDENT] infer-gateway elevated p95 observed at 15:12 UTC. Scope: single region/us-west-2; affected tenants: 12% of production traffic. Mitigation: attached +8 warm-pool slots and enabled temporary priority lanes. Current p95: 180ms. Owner: @oncall-inference. Postmortem scheduled: 2025-02-05."

Customer-facing (for impacted customers only):
We observed elevated response times for a subset of requests between 15:10–15:40 UTC. Our engineers applied a targeted mitigation to restore normal service levels and there is no data loss. We will follow up with details in the incident summary.

Headroom Negotiation Procedure (SRE + Product + Capacity PM)
-----------------------------------------------------------
Use this decision flow when the SRE oncall proposes temporary headroom credit beyond automatic policy: 
1) SRE prepares a short rationale doc (2–3 bullets): scope, estimated extra tokens or slots, rollback criteria, customer impact if not applied.
2) Convene 10-minute "Headroom Call" with Product and Capacity PMs. Share live dashboards and confirm rollback triggers.
3) If approved, apply headroom for a limited window (max 60 minutes) and assign an owner to monitor.
4) After window, SRE files a micro-incident review with metrics showing credit usage and a recommended remediation (scale, model optimization, billing adjustment).

Incident Review and Postmortem Standards
---------------------------------------
For intermittent degradations that consumed >=5% of SLO error budget or lasted >30 minutes, the incident review must include:
- Timeline with timestamps and decision points (who, what, why).
- Root-cause analysis with evidence: relevant traces, heatmaps, and deploy logs.
- Quantitative impact: % of error budget consumed, token cost delta, and affected tenant list.
- Remediation plan with owners and dates (e.g., increase warm pool by X by YYYY-MM-DD, implement KV prewarm on deploy).
- Follow-up evals: targeted Canary Evals (prompt sets) to ensure fallback model quality.

Metrics to capture in the review (minimum):
| Metric | Query/Source | Baseline | Incident Peak | Post-mitigation |
|-------|--------------|---------:|--------------:|---------------:|
| p95 latency (infer-gateway) | Prometheus (http_request_duration_seconds) | 160ms | 420ms | 180ms |
| 5xx rate | Prometheus (http_requests_total) | 0.02% | 0.6% | 0.05% |
| Warm-pool utilization | ops-api /warm-pool | 42% | 98% | 50% |
| Error budget consumed | SLO-ledger | 2.1% | 11.7% | 11.7% |

Continuous Improvements (examples)
--------------------------------
- Add a dedicated "degradation canary" synthetic test that simulates cold cache conditions for the top 10 models during deployment windows.
- Automate headroom decision checklist into the incident UI (pre-populate rationale fields and automated rollback timers).
- Improve telemetry by tagging traces with model-variant and tenant priority at ingestion to speed triage.

Owners and Escalation Contacts
-----------------------------
- SRE oncall: inference rotation (pager)
- Platform PM (capacity): @platform-capacity
- Product owner (top models): product-models team
- Oncall escalation matrix is maintained at: /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process

Appendices
----------
A. Quick PromQL snippets (for alert validation)
- p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"infer-gateway\"}[5m])) by (le))
- cache miss ratio: sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_request_total[5m]))

B. Triage checklist (printable one-pager)
1) Validate alert and scope
2) Correlate deploys
3) Check warm pool and batcher queue
4) Decide path: absorb / degrade / shape / fallback
5) Communicate internal + customers as needed

C. Sample incident timeline entry (format for postmortem)
"2025-01-28T15:12Z — Alert fired: 95th latency > 300ms (oncall acknowledged). 15:18Z — +8 warm pool slots attached (opsctl). 15:22Z — p95 reduced to 210ms; opened Headroom Call. 15:35Z — priority lanes enabled; p95 at 185ms. 16:10Z — mitigation stable; start 1-hour observation window."

Document maintenance
--------------------
- Owner: SRE inference stewardship (monthly review).
- Review cadence: every quarter or after any incident that consumes >10% of error budget.
- Change log: 2025-02-03 — clarified headroom thresholds and added rollback examples.
